bubbles.value_available_per_house: No. The store holds one radar value per 1 km cell (hail/t shards; summary.py rows radar_max and radar_1in), not per house. The 390 px block view covers 4 cells. Largest radar hail in the five seasons: 0.39 in, 0.31 in, 0.26 in, and none (no radar day of 0.25 in or more). No cell has a day of 1 inch or more in the five seasons, so a count of 1-inch days would read 0 in all four. A per-house figure cannot come from this store.
bubbles.same_value_shared_by_neighbours: Yes. The 250 houses in the view sit in those 4 cells: 62, 56, 66 and 66 houses. Every house in a cell would print the same number, so the bubbles would show 4 values in total, one of them missing.
bubbles.label_fit_estimate: No. At zoom 17 a dot is about 8 px across, and the median nearest-neighbour distance between dots is 19 CSS px (10th percentile 14 px). 98 percent of dots have a neighbour within 40 px. A 5 to 7 character label in the map's 13 px bold type is roughly 40 to 55 px wide, so labels would overlap on almost every house. Only a thinned subset could be labelled. The reference's own bubbles overlap in places (for example 477K under 520K).
bubbles.budget_note: Per-building value labels in the building shards would add about 9.8 raw bytes and 0.3 gzip bytes per building. The 4 shard files that hold this view go from 76,330 to 77,002 gzip bytes (+672, +0.9 percent). Reading the 2 radar cell shards that cover the view instead costs 2,046 gzip bytes and changes no building shard. The phone budget in data/map.json is 700,000 gzip bytes; I did not measure the full page load with labels added.

result.summary:
Nine map views (2 to 10) are matched to the owner's reference screenshots. View 9 is inside our map bounds, so it is included even though the brief said eight. Each view has a side-by-side PNG in /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/views/ (reference left, ours right, same height, one caption line with zoom and extent). Our captures are map-only (controls, legend, timeline, banners and attribution hidden) at 390x844, device scale factor 2, from the local build in /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/site. The layer menu and a hail sheet opened by a tap on 345 Blaine Street at zoom 17 are saved too (layers-menu-ours-390x844.png, hail-sheet-block-tap-390x844.png, and a three-panel comparison layers-and-sheet-side-by-side.png).

Block view: the reference frame is about 235 m across (zoom about 17.4). That comes from the store's own street geometry (hail/r roads shards for Brooks, Blaine and East Florence) fitted to the reference labels, residuals under 2 m. Our top zoom is 17 (319 m across), so the block view cannot match the reference extent. The page shows 249 dots at zoom 17: 248 outlines with address lines and 1 unmatched address dot.

Bubble question: the store can print one radar value per 1 km cell, not per house. The block view spans 4 cells. Labels would overlap for nearly every house at zoom 17. Per-building labels would add about 0.3 gzip bytes per building (0.9 percent on the four shards the view reads), or about 2 kB if the two radar cell shards are read instead.

Main gaps are data and design, not only zoom: our base map is white with Natural Earth roads, rivers, lakes, counties and places only. It has no land colour, parks, terrain, points of interest, route shields, reservation or forest shapes. At zooms 11 to 13 it shows little beyond the town bubbles. The layer menu lists weather layers, hail layers, Map or Imagery, and two toggles (warnings, storm reports). The reference menu lists map types, climate-risk and amenity chips, a points-of-interest toggle and a reset.

Sources and checks: reference files under /root/.claude/uploads/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/ (viewed). Site data under /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/site (data/map.json, hail/t, hail/b, hail/r, static/map/basemap.json). Code under /home/user/wt/wt-b5: website/summary.py lines 79-80 and 216-218, website/static/map/map.js lines 5792-5808 (tile boxes and quarters) and 5700-5727 (test hook), website/static/map/map.css lines 644 and 654. Views 4 to 8 extents are estimates, not measurements. View 4 uses the Rockin Rudy's point from view 3 and the Missoula city point; view 5 uses the same city points plus the University of Montana position; view 6 also uses the airport coordinates 46.9164, -114.0906 from memory, not checked against a source. Views 9 and 10 use Billings, Great Falls, Helena and Missoula from the site's own data (data/map.json places and website/towns.json). Their scale check (Montana's state borders in the reference) agrees within a few percent.

The local build is pinned to --now 2026-10-17T12:00:00Z (build.log), so the page's first screen shows the about 8 days old banner and the hail swath problem banner. The layer menu and hail sheet captures include these banners; the composites do not.

The reference shows price-style bubbles that overlap each other. The store cannot supply per-house values; the owner should decide whether a per-cell value is the thing to show, and how to label it.

result.summary: Six map chips were checked against live sources and our own store: Hail, Heat, Wind, Flood, Fire and Air. Ready now from our own store: Hail (MRMS radar estimate of hail 1 inch or more; 144,522 of 450,765 Montana cells had at least one such day in five years; one palette PNG of about 42 KB covers Montana at native cell size and can be placed like the radar frames), Heat (NOAA nClimGrid-Daily grid estimate of days at or above 90 F; the Billings cell matches the airport record within 2 days for July 2021 to June 2022) and Wind (NWS high wind and wind advisory products by public forecast zone; 83 public zones in the current edition; station gusts are airport points, 1,261 station days at 50 knots or more). Flood: the store holds 43 flood warning, 37 areal flood warning, 35 flood watch, 10 flood advisory and 548 areal flood advisory rows, and 277 Montana river gauges have live NWS flood categories, but FEMA flood zones are left out by repo decision D38 (a hazard and insurance designation) and the FEMA terms could not be read here; the FEMA layer has 31,335 polygons in the Montana box. Fire: the NIFC current perimeter service (5 perimeters in the box, newest updated 2026-10-21) and historic service (6,879 in the box) are live; the USGS MTBS national perimeter zip (390 MB) says there are no restrictions on use beyond acknowledgement; the 2023 USFS wildfire hazard potential raster (351 MB zip) says it can be used without additional permissions or fees. Air: the EPA AirNow API returns 401 without a key, so it needs an account; NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke polygons are live (116 polygons for 2026-10-24) but their public domain status is not verified; PurpleAir terms could not be read. Every legend must say the source, the estimate type and the data age; no chip may say no risk; missing data shows as data unavailable. Notes: notes.md was not written because the agent rules forbid report .md files; the commands, quotes and sizes are in /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/risk-sources/evidence.txt (plain text), and the sample downloads were deleted after measuring (the label folder is 2.2 MB, holding small saved pages and the scripts).
blockers: FEMA NFHL terms not read: the FEMA disclaimer page returned 403 (a content delivery network block page) to curl and 404 to the fetch tool; the flood-zone page returned 403; the Map Service Center home is a shell. The repo's own record says the flood-zone wording needs counsel first (DECISIONS.md line 941, counsel item 12). Do not build a FEMA layer until the owner and counsel decide.

PurpleAir terms and API documentation not readable: the terms page gave only a heading to the fetch tool and a 77-character shell to curl; the API pages are client-side shells. Licence, key rules and commercial use are unverified, so PurpleAir must not be used until its terms are read.
AirNow data terms and price not verified: the request without a key returns 401; the About page has no reuse text; the docs page does not state a price.
NOAA Hazard Mapping System public domain status not verified: the OSPO page has no reuse statement, the NOAA disclaimer page has no public domain text, and the NWS disclaimer covers NWS pages only.

USGS flood inundation maps not read: the USGS flood inundation page and the USGS copyright page returned 403 (block pages). Only one Montana gauge (CFMM8, Flathead River at Columbia Falls) has NWS inundation mapping enabled, out of 277 Montana gauges checked.

Wildfire hazard potential: the reuse sentence is verified ('can be used without additional permissions or fees') but the words 'public domain' do not appear; the Montana portion was not extracted from the 351 MB national zip, and the raster format inside the zip was not listed. The Wildfire Risk to Communities methods page does not name the raster, so the link from that site to the raster is unverified.

MTBS: Montana portion and burn severity rasters not measured (only the national perimeter zip, 389,925,218 bytes, was sized and read). The direct-download site moved to the Burn Severity site and the mtbs.gov page announces an outage starting 2026-10-28 at 8:00 PM for maintenance.

Sizes marked as rough are extrapolations from 200-feature samples (FEMA flood zones about 1.3 GB and NIFC historic perimeters about 104 MB as GeoJSON at full geometry); the full layers were not downloaded.

Storage: D38 (wt-b5 DECISIONS.md, the budget paragraph near line 815) records that all of hail/ breaks its caps (162.0 MB against 60 MB; j/ with j/e 86.2 MB against 40 MB) and that the owner or supervisor rules on both. A PNG layer would avoid shipping the 32 MB radar shard set to the browser for the hail chip, but the ruling still decides what ships.

claims.claim: A per-cell choropleth can be computed in one pass over the shards. Cell row = r*10 + key//10 and column = c*10 + key%10, using the shard name and the in-tile key. Row 0 is centred at 54.995 N and column 0 at 129.995 W, so a cell centre is (54.995 - row/100, -129.995 + col/100). Days = count of stored values at or above 254 tenths; largest = maximum stored value.
claims.evidence: hail.py docstring grid rule (row 0 at 54.995 N, column 0 at 129.995 W, 0.01 degree cells, 10 by 10 cells per tile; key = (row % 10) * 10 + (col % 10)). The count script uses the same arithmetic and returns 428,843 cells.
claims.size_or_cadence: Store rebuilt by the build; as_of 2026-10-16.
claims.checked_how: Read the rule in hail.py; the render_test.py output shows 428,843 non-empty pixels, the same count as the store.

result.reason: Refuted as written. The store is real and intact, its source is NOAA MRMS MESH, and its values match the raw NOAA file cell for cell for the one day checked, so the capability holds. The claim fails on currency and wording. (1) Out of date: the copy it cites (as_of 2026-10-16) is nine days old on 2026-10-25, past the page's own three-day stale limit (STALE_DAYS = 3). NOAA already publishes SPC days 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-24, which that copy lacks. The production store the site reads (hail-store-main.tar.gz) has as_of 2026-10-23 and window 2021-10-24 to 2026-10-23, so the claim's window and as_of are not current figures. (2) Licence: "NOAA data" is true but incomplete. NOAA's registry page asks for attribution, bars implied endorsement, and says modified data may not be presented as original, unaltered NOAA data. The NOAA page at noaa.gov/disclaimer covers external links and has no data licence text. (3) Units: the cited user table, UserTable_MRMS_v12.2, could not be retrieved. "Millimetres" is supported by the raw values and a WDTD page, but not checked against the table. (4) Source label: four days (2025-06-25, 2025-06-26, 2026-05-25, 2026-09-10) are rebuilt from two-minute frames, and 2025-06-25 is partial (717 of 720 frames). The "MESH_Max_1440min_00.50" label does not say so, though copy_check does.

(2) 'Disclaimer only' holds for the current item and its NIFC siblings, not for the family. The page also says "GIS files for all Wildfire Risk to Communities data are available for download by state at the Forest Service Research Data Archive." So the page does link to raster data, which the claim missed.

3. The DOI resolves (HTTP 200) to https://www.fs.usda.gov/rds/archive/catalog/RDS-2020-0016-2. Title: "Wildfire Risk to Communities: Spatial datasets of landscape-wide wildfire risk components for the United States (2nd Edition)", publication year 2024. It lists "RDS-2020-0016-2__WHP_CONUS.zip (8.17 GB" and "RDS-2020-0016-2_Montana.zip (11.4 GB", both linked to usfs-public.box.com shared files. The file index (https://www.fs.usda.gov/rds/archive/products/RDS-2020-0016-2/_fileindex_RDS-2020-0016-2.html) says: "WHP_[EXTENT].tif: Continuous integer values of the Wildfire Hazard Potential index with a 30 m pixel size."

4. Zip content: a ranged GET (bytes 0-63) of the CONUS link returned HTTP 206 with a zip header. A HEAD request returned 404, so HEAD is not a valid check for these links. The zip central directories list "WHP_CONUS/WHP_CONUS.tif" (zip size 8,774,416,139 bytes, which is 8.17 GiB) and "MT/WHP_MT.tif" (zip size 12,270,052,354 bytes). Both WHP TIFF headers are BigTIFF (magic 43). I did not download the full rasters.

5. Excel (https://wildfirerisk.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/wrc_download_20260415.xlsx): 4,968,274 bytes, matching the claim. Sheets are README, METADATA, States, Counties, Communities and Tribal Areas, so the claim leaves out two. The only hyperlink is README to the methods page. There is no doi.org, archive or raster link. The 3 "Hazard" hits are place names (Hazardville, CT; Hazard, KY; Hazard, NE). The claim is right that the workbook has no raster link.

6. Legacy service (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/fsgisx01/rest/services/RDW_Wildfire/RMRS_WRC_WildfireHazardPotential/ImageServer?f=json): HTTP 403. Body: "Error: The service being requested has been migrated to IIPP. Please visit https://imagery.geoplatform.gov/iipp/rest/services." The claim omitted that address.

7. Migrated service (https://imagery.geoplatform.gov/iipp/rest/services/Fire_Aviation/USFS_EDW_RMRS_WRC_WildfireHazardPotential/ImageServer?f=json), JSON read with python in isolated mode: pixel size 30, pixel type U16, raster functions "WHP" and "None", description "the 2024 version of components of wildfire risk". The RDW_Wildfire folder returns "Folder not found" on the new host, so the new path differs from the old one. Identify queries returned WHP integers 25 (MT, -111.9, 45.7), 145 (MT, -114.0, 46.9) and 35 (KS, -98.5, 39.5), and NoData at four populated-area points (-112.04, 46.59; -104.8, 39.7; -80.2, 25.8; -116.2, 43.6). getSamples returned an error body at those same four points; I did not establish why.

8. Licence (the claim says "n/a"): the catalog says "These data were collected using funding from the U.S. Government and can be used without additional permissions or fees." The open-access use terms (https://www.fs.usda.gov/rds/archive/datauseinfo/open) require citation and error notification, forbid re-distributing a modified version "as the original data publication", and include a distribution-liability clause. The claim's "n/a" is wrong.

9. Size and vintage (the claim says "n/a"): the catalog gives 8.17 GB and 11.4 GB, which match the zip sizes in GiB. It gives "Publication Year: 2024" and "2nd Edition".

10. Unresolved caveat: the FGDC metadata inside each zip (WHP_CONUS.tif.xml and WHP_MT.tif.xml) says "16 Bit unsigned integer", but also "Values for CONUS are between 0 and 98,165", "Values for Montana are between 0 and 70367" and "In practice, the maximum value is 99,853". A 16-bit unsigned value cannot exceed 65,535, and the migrated service is also U16. Values above 65,535 should be checked before the layer is used.

Conclusion: the site links to the hazard raster through the download page, the archive and the migrated service, and I checked all three. The claim's conclusion is therefore wrong.
